cases.observation: Valid order {customerId:1, orderTotal.amount:12.34} -> 200 {"orderId":2}. Read-back: orders row id=2 customer_id=1 amount=12.34 PENDING; message row with destination=Order class name (65 chars), headers length 391, payload length 63 = {"orderDetails":{"customerId":1,"orderTotal":{"amount":12.34}}}.

cases.observation: orderTotal.amount sent as a 942-character JSON number (1.000...0001) so the serialized OrderCreatedEvent payload is exactly 1000 characters -> 200 {"orderId":3}. Read-back: message.payload LENGTH=1000, stored intact (tail ...000000001}}}); orders.amount rounded by DECIMAL(38,2) to 1.00 (not a target column).

evidence.description: C03-violation-payload-1001: request/response with DB before/after counts and read-back
C03-violation-payload-1001: correlated order-service log slice (Hibernate SQL, JdbcTemplate binds, exceptions)

cases.observation: Payload of 1001 characters: orders insert executed (Hibernate log), then insert into eventuate.message failed with MysqlDataTruncation "Data too long for column 'payload' at row 1" (DataIntegrityViolationException, logged by MessageProducerImpl 'Sending failed'). Response is generic 500 {"error":"Internal Server Error"}. Transaction rolled back: orders/message counts unchanged (2/2) and orders id 4 was consumed but never persisted (AUTO_INCREMENT gap).

evidence.description: C04-violation-payload-1500: request/response with DB before/after counts and read-back
C04-violation-payload-1500: correlated order-service log slice (Hibernate SQL, JdbcTemplate binds, exceptions)

cases.observation: Payload target 1500 chars required a 1442-char number; Jackson rejected it before the controller (HttpMessageNotReadableException: Number value length (1441) exceeds the maximum allowed (1000)). No SQL issued. Pre-persistence failure unrelated to the predicate; bounds the attack window to payloads of 1001..~1058 chars via this field.

C05-client-supplied-order-id: correlated order-service log slice (Hibernate SQL, JdbcTemplate binds, exceptions)

cases.observation: Body includes "id":2 and "orderId":2 (an existing order id) plus customerId 7. CreateOrderRequest(customerId, orderTotal) silently ignores them; Hibernate insert omits id (IDENTITY) and a new id 5 was generated. Read-back: order 2 unchanged, new row id=5 customer_id=7 amount=5.00. Duplicate PK cannot be forced via the API.
